headline: Shabwa Camp Toll Rises to 73 Dead
deck: Authorities say 14 people remain missing after the camp strike; Britain has announced defensive RAF support for Saudi Arabia.
body: Shabwa authorities said the death toll from Monday's missile attack on a military camp has risen to 73, with 14 people still missing. Shabwa governor Awad Ibn al-Wazir told the Associated Press that the recruits were aged 18 to 20 and that some remained missing. [E5][E6]
On 20 October, this paper reported that Shabwa authorities said more than 53 recruits had been killed and more than 200 injured. [E7]

Britain said it will provide additional defensive military support to Saudi Arabia and fly RAF Typhoon counter-air missions to protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure from aerial attack. The government said the Typhoons will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis. [E1][E2][E3]
AP reported that Britain is also sending a military transport and an unspecified number of military advisers, and has extended its offer of in-air refuelling for Saudi aircraft by 90 days. [E4]
